> > >     exp(Wv)), log = TRUE) + log(pnoRet)
> > >   RTMB::ADREPORT(ll * wHvar)
> > >   return(sum(ll * wHvar))
> > > }

messages.subject: Laplace approximation using RTMB and integrate yield different results
messages.subject_clean: Laplace approximation using RTMB and integrate yield different results
messages.body_plain:
I am giving a try to the laplae approximation using the RTMB package and compare the results with the integrate function in R.

Surprisingly I get different results and was wondering if I am making a mistake somewhere.

Here is my R code:

mustar <- 1.2
sigmastar <- 0.6
# Laplace approximation
LA_w <- MakeADFun(function(varW) {
  getAll(varW, warn = FALSE)
  1/2 * (exp(w) - mustar)^2/sigmastar^2 - w
}, list(w = 0, mustar = mustar, sigmastar = sigmastar), random = "w",
silent = TRUE)
LA_w$fn()
# Using integrate
GK_w <- integrate(f = function(w, mustar, sigmastar) {
    exp(-1/2 * (exp(w) - mustar)^2/sigmastar^2 + w)
  }, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf, subdivisions = 100, mustar = mustar,
  sigmastar = sigmastar, rel.tol = 1e-06, stop.on.error = FALSE)$value

-log(GK_w)

messages.subject: bit weird behavior with RTMB?
messages.body_plain:
I'm new to RTMB, so a problem I've experienced is probably just from naivete, not from an issue with RTMB. I've coded up an objective function in R that calls a couple of other functions (might or might not  be relevant). The source for all the functions involved is in a separate file from the script I run to MakeADFun of the objective function. If I source the file with the objective function code and MakeADFun it, everything works fine. However, if I source the code, run the objective function code as an R function (i.e., without having MakeADFun'd it first), and then MakeADFun it, I get the error "Error in advector(e1) : Invalid argument to 'advector' (lost class attribute?)". If I then remove the sourced functions, source the code again, and just run MakeADFun I get no error message and everything seems fine.

So my question is: Is this expected behavior? I.e., don't run your objective function as an R function before MakeADFun'ing it? Hopefully the answer is simply "yes, you dummy, you must have missed it in the help files".

Cheers!

William T. Stockhausen

Research Fishery Biologist, Alaska Fisheries Science Center

NOAA Fisheries | U.S. Department of Commerce

Office: (206) 526-4241

www.fisheries.noaa.gov <http://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/>

messages.subject: Can we detect a harbinger from the outcome of "MakeADFun" before "nlminb"?
messages.subject_clean: Can we detect a harbinger from the outcome of "MakeADFun" before "nlminb"?
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

I have a loop (i.e., many iterations), where there is an estimation stage with “MakeADFun” and “nlminb” per iteration.  Often the loop crashes with “nlminb”.  The associated error message is:

   Error in nlminb(model$par, model$fn, model$gr, upper = unlist(Up_bound),  :

        NA/NaN gradient evaluation

where “model” is the object, which is made with “MakeADFun”.   Such a crash forcefully stopped the loop.  This is the major problem, which made me consult you in this email.

Is there any way to skip a crash and to let the loop continue to run?  In other words, can we detect a harbinger from the outcome of MakeADFun, which would lead to a crash with “nlminb”?   For example, if I could detect a crash case with the outcome of MakeADFun *before* reaching “nlminb” inside each loop run, I would put an if-else statement to avoid passing the crash case to “nlminb”.

I would greatly appreciate your tips and advice.

Saang-Yoon
